solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cigarette's harmful, principally: my one tip to reform smoker

indicators.note: principally points to the chief, leading letter of each of the two words before it
to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An anti-smoking message: cigarettes are harmful, so take my advice and give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' looks like part of the health warning but is the definition. 'principally' gives C and H; 'reform' rearranges MY ONE TIP into IMNEYPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the pot on top of a flue is what visibly puffs out smoke from a house.

clue.text: More difficult saving nothing — for this person?

definitions.text: More difficult saving nothing — for this person?

indicators.note: saving here means holding on to, so the word for more difficult keeps something inside it

parts.note: harder means more difficult
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone finding it harder to save any money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone who saves everything and throws nothing away. 'saving' puts O inside HARDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stockpiles and keeps things would find it hard to save nothing at all.

clue.text: Exploit dairy produce

definitions.meaning: to exploit is to take every possible advantage from something, as a verb
the white drink that comes from cows

explanation.surface: A complaint that farmers' dairy goods are being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: drawing every drop from a cow, and squeezing every advantage from a situation.

clue.text: Catch some violent rapscallions

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrest a few dangerous rogues.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone, as with a trap, is to catch them.

clue.text: Stopped working and prepared to leave?

definitions.meaning: a machine that has broken down is said to have given up or conked out
someone who has put belongings in bags is ready to go; the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.surface: Someone who has downed tools and is getting ready to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a failed engine has died; literally, someone with bags full is ready to depart.

clue.text: Drinks served to English guy

parts.note: cups of tea are drinks

explanation.surface: Someone's beverages are brought to an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, but here it is a verb: to mock or make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old verb for ridiculing or mocking them, i.e. to rib them playfully.

clue.text: TV presenter answered differently, with some hesitation

indicators.note: arranged differently means the letters of the word before are put in another order

parts.note: er is the sound a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: A television host replied in an unexpected way, pausing a little.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who reads out bulletins on a television channel is a kind of presenter.

clue.text: Small apartment, dull, to rent out

parts.note: flat means dull, lacking interest
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blunt listing: a small, boring apartment available to rent.
explanation.definitionFit: The diminutive suffix makes a little dwelling: a small set of rooms in a building.

clue.text: Gift distributed by female reps

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread around and put down in a new order

explanation.surface: Sales representatives handing out presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges FEMALE REPS; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A product given away for nothing to try is a promotional present.

clue.text: Run after husband when entering church

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the pieces before it go inside the word for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A wedding scene: someone dashes after the groom as he walks into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like the start of the action, but 'Run after' together is the definition; CE (Church of England) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue something is to run after it.

clue.text: Edible plant partly wolfed down

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A vegetable that was half eaten greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro, a tropical plant with a starchy root, is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Without vehicle, touring capital of Egypt is irresponsible

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the words for lacking a vehicle surround the letter

parts.note: car-less means having no car, a vehicle

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tourist travelling through Cairo without a car is being reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without proper thought or caution is the same as being heedless or irresponsible.

clue.text: Waders nipped small sea birds

parts.note: bit means nipped with the teeth
terns are small seabirds

explanation.surface: Wading birds pecking at gulls on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waders' could be boots, but it means birds that wade in marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are heron-like marsh birds that wade in reed beds, famed for a booming call.

clue.text: Son taking school test fully

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A boy sitting a thorough exam at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to teach or coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something to its limit, as with a rope or one's patience, is to test it fully.

clue.text: Fellow after mainly fast food

indicators.note: after places the word for fellow behind the shortened word
mainly means most of a word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: quick means fast
he is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in search of mostly fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as one phrase, but 'fast' is wordplay and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An open savoury tart of eggs and cream is a dish, an example of food.

clue.text: Cruel MP's unexpected collapse

indicators.note: unexpected suggests letters turning up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A heartless politician suddenly falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', a link; 'unexpected' rearranges CRUEL MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold in on oneself, crushed, is to give way or collapse.

clue.text: Conflict in the main upset inexperienced medic

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
doc is a doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A green young doctor upset by a clash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RAWDOC. 'the main' is an old word for the open sea; the Cod Wars were 1950s-70s fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the naval fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland, a conflict fought at sea.

clue.text: Hat Norma ruined in race

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A woman named Norma has her hat spoiled during a running event.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance running event over about 26 miles is a famous race.

clue.text: Went on journey, you say? Took boat

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is to be taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: rode means travelled, went on a journey on horse or in a car

explanation.surface: A traveller asking if someone went on a trip, then confirming they went by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling oars, someone took a boat out on the water.

clue.text: Leader abandons group of soldiers in parade ground

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is left off the word

parts.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers

explanation.surface: The officer walks away from a unit drilling in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle, an enclosed courtyard, can serve as a square for parading on.

clue.text: What's needed for exam success? I can't answer that

definitions.meaning: a mark that lets you through a test
what a quiz contestant says to skip a question

explanation.definitionFit: A grade that gets you through a test, and the word quiz contestants say to move on.

clue.text: Cut top off rose, for instance

indicators.note: top off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a rose is an example of a flower

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on deadheading a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a gardening instruction, but it is the definition: to reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce prices or rates is to cut them, bringing them down.

clue.text: Western pop artist's cover?

parts.note: a rapper is a popular music artist

explanation.surface: Asking about an American pop singer's album cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wound around an item, like paper round a sweet, is a protective covering.

clue.text: Puddings I'd sent back, upset

indicators.note: sent back means the words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: puddings are desserts
I'd is written as ID

explanation.surface: A diner is troubled after returning the puddings to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious or troubled is the same as being upset.
